title: Burnt Butter Hazelnut Cookies
story: These cookies were the first recipe we built together. They taught us that little choices matter—blooming a spice, browning butter a shade darker than feels safe, waiting an extra hour for the dough to rest. They're proof that care isn't complicated. It's just a series of small decisions that add up to something people remember.

items.text: ½ tsp ground cardamom (bloomed in butter)

steps.text: Melt ½ cup unsalted butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
steps.donenessCue: Butter turns deep amber and smells deeply nutty — go a shade darker than feels safe.

steps.text: Remove from heat immediately. Stir in 1 tsp fresh orange zest and ½ tsp ground cardamom. Blooming the cardamom in the warm fat draws out its aromatic oils for a deeper, rounder flavor — the other ½ tsp goes in with the dry ingredients to keep its brighter, more fragrant notes.
Set aside and let the brown butter cool completely to room temperature before continuing.
In a medium bowl, whisk together 1 cup hazelnut meal, ½ cup all-purpose flour, ½ tsp baking powder, ¼ tsp fine salt, and ½ tsp ground cardamom. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the cooled brown butter, ½ cup dark brown sugar, and ¼ cup white sugar. Beat until smooth and creamy.
Beat in 1 large room-temperature egg and 1 tsp vanilla extract until fully combined.
Fold in the dry ingredients just until no dry spots remain. Do not overmix.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. This is required — do not skip.
Scoop approximately 1½ tablespoons of dough per cookie. Roll gently into balls and flatten slightly.

steps.donenessCue: Edges are golden brown and centers look set — not glossy or wet.

steps.text: Cool on the baking sheet for 5–7 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. The flavor noticeably deepens after 12–24 hours.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Add ½ teaspoon honey or ½ teaspoon molasses to the sugars for a darker, more caramelized flavor.
Sprinkle with flaky sea salt while the cookies are still warm for a sweet-and-savory finish.
Fold in ¼ cup chopped toasted hazelnuts before chilling the dough for a little extra texture.
storage: Store loosely covered at room temperature. The flavor noticeably deepens after 12–24 hours.
